correctness.rationale: Signed Laplacian L_s=nI-J-2L_H gives W_n(S)=(1/n)prod_{i=2}^n(n-2lambda_i(H)) by weighted matrix tree, including singular cases by polynomial continuity. For a graph with k negative edges, each nontrivial connected component has at most k+1 vertices; complement Laplacian positivity bounds lambda_max<=k+1. Equality requires one (k+1)-vertex tree and disconnected complement, which forces a star. At n=2p, all k0; at k=p-1 zero iff K_{1,p-1} with p isolates. Count n*binom(n-1,p-1), dividing by two at n=4. For odd n all Walsh sums have Cayley parity one and cannot vanish. Independently checked signed cofactors for n=6 across 0,1,2 negative edges, recovering first zero at 2 with 60 cases; finite n does not substitute for all-n proof.
residual_risks: An older algebraic-graph-spectral statement may include this k-edge zero threshold as an unstated corollary; searched published records do not show it.
Finite checks were inspected and one independent small-order cofactor enumeration performed; large-n correctness rests on the analytic eigenvalue proof.
No complete higher-weight zero set or sharp endpoint ell^1 norms are proved.
